items.title: Lego to build €1bn factory in Portugal, its eighth worldwide
items.why: Danish toymaker Lego will build a factory in Estarreja, near Aveiro in northern Portugal, investing about €1bn and creating more than 1,000 jobs, it announced on Monday. Construction starts in 2027 and brick production in 2030. It will be Lego's fourth factory in Europe.

items.title: CrowdStrike agrees to buy rival Zscaler for $43.9bn
items.why: US cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike will buy Zscaler in an all-share deal valuing it at about $43.9bn, the companies said on Monday. Zscaler shareholders get a 34% premium. The deal needs shareholder and regulatory approval and is expected to close in CrowdStrike's 2028 financial year.
items.matters: Euronews calls it the biggest cybersecurity deal ever, combining two firms that protect many large organisations.

items.title: India pledges $1.6bn to help flood-hit Nepal rebuild
items.why: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a 240 billion Nepali rupee (about $1.6bn) package in New Delhi on Monday during a visit by Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah. Nepal's August glacier flood killed about 1,500 people, and 5,200 are missing, Reuters reports.
items.matters: Nepal puts rebuilding costs at about three times India's offer, so it still needs much more help.

items.title: Belgian airports halt flights as unions strike against government cuts
items.why: Air traffic controllers joined a national day of union action on Monday, halting flights at Brussels and Charleroi airports from 07:00 to 21:00 local time. About 59,500 passengers had been booked on 429 Brussels flights. Unions oppose Prime Minister Bart De Wever's austerity budget.
items.matters: Airlines say it is the 11th strike affecting Belgian airspace in 11 months.

items.title: Molly Meldrum, Australian music presenter and Countdown host, dies at 83
items.why: Ian 'Molly' Meldrum died in hospital in Melbourne on Monday morning after a period of declining health, his management said. He hosted ABC TV's music show Countdown from 1974 to 1987, helping to launch Australian acts and bring stars such as ABBA and Madonna to Australian audiences.
items.matters: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and many musicians paid tribute to a figure who shaped Australian pop for decades.

items.title: Asian shares fall after AI sell-off drives Wall Street into correction
items.why: South Korea's Kospi closed 3.3% lower on Monday, after falling more than 5% at one point. On Friday the Nasdaq dropped 5.3%, wiping out its 2026 gains, and the S&P 500 fell 3.7%, more than 10% below its October peak. Nvidia shares fell about 13%.
items.matters: Investors fear tech firms' huge AI spending may not pay off, and the falls touch savings and pensions worldwide.

items.title: Thailand's Jeeno Thitikul wins LPGA Tour Championship for third year running
items.why: Jeeno Thitikul shot a bogey-free 65 to win the season-ending CME Group Tour Championship in Naples, Florida, on Sunday by two shots from Japan's Aki Iwai. The $4m prize, the biggest in women's golf, made her the LPGA's all-time top earner.
items.matters: She passed Annika Sörenstam's career prize-money record, which had stood for 25 years.

items.title: Democrats win largest US House majority since 1992 after recount
items.why: Democrat Chuck Hubbard won North Carolina's 5th district after a recount, beating long-serving Republican Virginia Foxx by about 330 votes. That gives Democrats at least 258 of the 435 House seats in the November midterms, their most since 1992. Four races are still undecided.
items.matters: A large majority lets Democrats control the House agenda and investigations for the second half of President Trump's term.

items.title: Fighting near Congo hospital traps health workers in Ebola outbreak zone
items.why: Health workers sheltered in a hospital maternity ward for more than 24 hours as fighting took place nearby in Ituri province, eastern DR Congo, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on Sunday. The WHO counts 11,613 confirmed cases and 5,678 deaths in the outbreak by 17 November.
items.matters: It is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak recorded in the country, and violence is making it harder to contain.

items.title: Alcaraz beats Zverev to win his first ATP Finals title
items.why: Spain's Carlos Alcaraz beat world number one Alexander Zverev of Germany 6-2, 7-6 in the ATP Finals final in Turin, Italy, on Sunday. He saved three set points in the tie-break and won all five of his matches. It is his 30th career title.
items.matters: He joins Agassi, Federer and Djokovic as the only men to win all four majors and the season-ending finals.

items.title: Netanyahu and Eisenkot parties end unity talks without a deal
items.why: Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud and Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party held more than four hours of coalition talks in Herzliya, Israel, on Sunday without agreement, and say they will meet again. They disagree over who would lead and over including far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir.
items.matters: Eisenkot has until 6 December, with a possible two-week extension, to form a government after October's election.

items.title: Liverpool beat ten-man Manchester United 4-0 in Pochettino's first game
items.why: Liverpool beat Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield on Sunday in Mauricio Pochettino's first match as United manager. Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Muñoz scored. United are 19th in the Premier League.

items.title: Poland says Russia twice plotted to kill Ukrainian-American rapper
items.why: Poland's foreign ministry says Russian intelligence tried to kill the rapper Kyivstoner in Poland in August, where a Russian citizen was detained. Denmark says it foiled a second plot at a concert near Copenhagen in September, charging two men and expelling a Russian diplomat. Russia calls the claims unsubstantiated.

items.changed: Updated: governments and Pacific nations react to the collapse
items.title: COP31 climate talks in Türkiye end without a deal over fossil fuels
items.why: The UN climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, ended on Sunday, two days late, without an agreed final text. Oil-producing states blocked any mention of moving away from fossil fuels, so the EU and others rejected it. UN chief António Guterres expressed 'profound frustration'.
items.matters: Al Jazeera says it is the first UN climate summit since Copenhagen in 2009 to end without a deal adopted by all.

items.title: New Hunger Games prequel opens with $225m worldwide box office
items.why: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping took an estimated $120m in North America and $105m in 84 other markets in its opening weekend, studio estimates show. It was the top film in the US despite competition from the launch of the video game Grand Theft Auto VI.

items.title: Istanbul officials hunt for lioness loose in forest on city's edge
items.why: Teams with thermal cameras and drones are searching woods in Uskumruköy, on Istanbul's northern edge, after a resident reported a lion on Sunday evening. Camera footage suggests a female lion. Officials say they want to capture it alive and have told residents to stay indoors.
items.matters: Keeping lions as pets is illegal in Türkiye; officials think it may have escaped from a private home.

items.title: Marc Márquez clinches eighth MotoGP world title in Portugal
items.why: Spain's Marc Márquez finished eighth at the Portuguese Grand Prix in Portimão on Sunday, enough to win his eighth premier-class title with one race left. Italy's Marco Bezzecchi won the race. Márquez had been 102 points behind Bezzecchi earlier in the season.
items.matters: He equals Giacomo Agostini's record of eight top-class titles and moves past Valentino Rossi's seven.

items.title: Thousands march in Istanbul against crackdown on opposition media
items.why: Several thousand people marched through Istanbul's Beşiktaş district on Sunday, called out by the opposition New Party (Yeni Parti). It followed a police raid on the pro-opposition broadcaster Sözcü TV, where a government-appointed trustee took control and senior staff were arrested. The government accuses some journalists of spreading 'fake news'.
items.matters: A media rights group, MLSA, says 25 journalists are currently jailed in Türkiye.

items.title: Delta software fault delays flights across US before Thanksgiving
items.why: A fault in Delta Air Lines' system for calculating aircraft weight and balance delayed more than 1,600 flights across the US on Sunday, mostly at its Atlanta hub, ABC News reports. Delta said the system was fixed later that day and the outage was not caused by a hack.
items.matters: US intelligence chief Jay Clayton warned of more 'glitches' as organisations upgrade systems after a run of US outages.

items.title: Gukesh and Sindarov open youngest-ever world chess title match in Geneva
items.why: India's Gukesh Dommaraju defends his world chess title against Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva, Switzerland. The opening ceremony is on Sunday and the first game on Tuesday 24 November. Both are 20, making it the youngest title match ever. The first to 7.5 points from 14 games wins.
items.matters: Sindarov is unbeaten against Gukesh in classical games; a win would make him Uzbekistan's first undisputed world champion.

items.title: Verstappen wins chaotic Las Vegas Grand Prix from pole
items.why: Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix by 0.639 seconds from McLaren's Lando Norris, with Oscar Piastri third. New champion Kimi Antonelli lost two places on the final lap to finish fourth. Ferrari team-mates Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collided again.
items.matters: It was Verstappen's 75th career win and lifts him to second in the drivers' standings.
items.changed: Updated: the race has been run and Verstappen won

items.title: Indonesia factory fire: 24 body bags recovered and dozens still missing
items.why: Rescuers had recovered 24 body bags from a burned sweets factory in Cikande, Banten province, west of Jakarta, by Sunday evening, officials say. Remains must be identified by DNA, which could take weeks. About 30 to 34 people are still missing, according to differing official counts.
items.changed: Updated: 24 body bags recovered; about 30 to 34 people still missing

items.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv region kill at least 15, Ukraine says
items.why: Russian strikes on Sunday killed at least 15 people in Ukraine's Kyiv region, officials say. Eleven died when a five-storey block partly collapsed in Dymer, north of the capital. Vyshneve's mayor says a strike on a supermarket killed three.
items.matters: President Zelensky says Russia fired about 2,700 drones and 165 missiles at Ukraine this week.
items.changed: Updated: the death toll rose to at least 15

items.title: Zelensky says Ukrainian sea drones sank Russian warship off Libya
items.why: President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday that seven Ukrainian sea drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi, eastern Libya, and hit the cargo ship Angara. Satellite images from the US firm Vantor show the warship capsized.
items.matters: It follows Saturday's drone strike on a Russian cargo ship in the Baltic, suggesting the war is reaching further from Ukraine.
items.changed: Updated: satellite images show the warship capsized

items.title: South Korea's education minister resigns over AI exam cheating fears
items.why: Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned on Sunday, and President Lee Jae Myung accepted. He took responsibility for last-minute rules to stop AI-assisted cheating in Thursday's Suneung university entrance exam. Officials say 111 test-takers were caught with smart devices.
items.matters: It began when a top scorer in a national accountancy exam admitted using a hidden camera and phone.

items.title: New Zealand hold on to draw first Test after India's record 720
items.why: New Zealand batted out the final day in Wellington to draw with India, finishing on 239 for five, still 113 runs behind, after following on. India had declared on 720 for nine, the highest Test total in New Zealand. The second Test starts in Christchurch on Friday.
items.changed: Updated: the match ended in a draw

items.title: Drone strikes kill four in Sudan's capital and damage UN building
items.why: Drone attacks early on Sunday killed at least four people in and around Khartoum, Sudan's capital, according to local reports, and damaged a UN building with staff inside, the UN says. The paramilitary Rapid Support Forces were blamed. Sudan's army says the drones came from Ethiopia, which denies it.

items.title: Settlers set Palestinian cars on fire in West Bank villages, reports say
items.why: Israeli settlers set fire to about 12 vehicles and sprayed slogans on homes in Kafr Malik, Deir Abu Mash'al and Deir al-Sudan, near Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, early on Sunday, Palestinian sources say. Israel's army condemned the attacks and police opened an investigation.

items.title: Iran vows to counter US blockade after strike on Bahrain
items.why: Iran's foreign ministry said on Monday that Tehran will 'use all available means' against the US naval blockade. On Sunday President Trump said Iranian ships trying to break it would go to the 'bottom of the sea'. Bahrain says an Iranian strike on Saturday wounded two.
items.matters: The strait carries a large share of the world's oil, so attacks there affect energy prices everywhere.
items.changed: Updated: Iran vowed to counter the US blockade after Trump's threat

items.title: BepiColombo spacecraft enters orbit around Mercury after eight-year journey
items.why: The European–Japanese BepiColombo mission entered orbit around Mercury on Saturday after a 37-minute engine burn, the European Space Agency says. It launched in 2018. The burn ended early because of a software issue, but ESA says the spacecraft is safe. Its two orbiters separate on 9–10 December.
items.matters: It is only the second mission to orbit Mercury, the planet closest to the Sun; science work starts in April 2027.

items.title: England beat New Zealand 37-12 for record win over All Blacks
items.why: England scored five tries to beat New Zealand 37-12 at Twickenham in London on Saturday in the Nations Championship. The 25-point margin is England's largest against the All Blacks and New Zealand's heaviest defeat in the northern hemisphere.

items.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal after ten years of talks
items.why: The European Union and Indonesia signed a trade agreement and an investment protection deal in Brussels on Saturday. Indonesia says 90.4% of its goods will enter the EU duty-free. The EU gains easier access to a market of 280 million people and to nickel for batteries.
items.matters: Both sides still need to ratify it; Indonesia expects it to take effect in 2027.

items.title: US media report hacks at FBI crime database and farm agency
items.why: The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its National Crime Information Center, used by police across the US, NBC News and CNN reported on Friday. Separately, a US Department of Agriculture system for paying farmers was hit by a cyberattack, officials said. It is unclear who is responsible.
items.matters: President Trump said on Saturday the reported FBI hack was 'not good' but might reveal things 'we would have never learned'.
items.changed: Updated: President Trump commented on the reported FBI hack

items.title: Poland says Russian missiles crashed on its soil near European drills
items.why: Poland says two Russian missiles and a drone fell on its territory on Friday during an attack on Ukraine, near Nowy Lipowiec, about 60km from the Ukrainian border. Nobody was hurt. In Warsaw on Saturday, NATO chief Mark Rutte said the alliance 'will defend every inch of Polish territory'.
items.matters: NATO's North Atlantic Council meets on Monday to discuss the incident, which Poland calls a deliberate provocation.
items.changed: Updated: NATO's chief pledged to defend Poland; NATO ambassadors meet in Brussels on Monday
